newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Demand falls on Bulgaria depo market after peg.
newsitem.headline: Demand falls on Bulgaria depo market after peg.

text.p: Demand for lev funds on the Bulgarian interbank market fell sharply but supply rose due to foreign currency sales as the interbank deposit rates fell from Monday, dealers said.
"Banks which had bought marks at lower rates, now sell them to the central bank," said a bank dealer.
The central bank was buying marks at 995 levs due to the introduction of a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 levs per mark along with the introduction of a currency board system on Tuesday, traders said.
Banks have been bidding for marks in the past few weeks, aiming for a larger profit from foreign currency sales at the fixed exchange rate rather than from buying treasury paper.

The average yield to maturity fell to 2.46 and 4.87 percent respectively at Monday's auctions of three- and six-month discount T-bills from 2.55 and 4.99 percent at the respective maturities auctioned on June 23.

Overnight interbank depo rates fell to 9-10 percent annually from 12-14 percent on Monday while deposits for up to seven days were borrowed at a simple annual interest of 7-8 percent, down from 10-12 percent.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 10.17 percent on Monday against 12.12 percent on Friday, a central bank official said. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
